payload.explanation: Finding from fire still_base1 at trigger_wall_ns 1793650247970930000, during place_inverted_u_yellow (a planned step). What I observed: base1's TF position had been within about 1.4 mm of its run-start pose (0.40278, -0.19857) through all three earlier seatings (0.0009 m after place_line_green). During the slow position-controlled descent of inverted_u_yellow (move_grasp_center_to_pose, started 1793650243121857000), finger_joint effort jumped from 63.4 to 115 at about 1793650246.09 s, and then to 143 at about 247.93 s. At the same time the seated stack broke apart, and base1 moved 0.0207 m (fire), reaching 0.0315 m at (0.40869, -0.16761) with a -1.4 deg yaw after release. Why it is a departure: base1 is the fixture. Contact with it is expected, but it must never be displaced, and it is now 0.0315 m from rest, beyond the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance. What I believe happened: the carried inverted_u_yellow met the already-seated parts about 3.9 cm above its seat height (part centre z 0.083 vs placement z 0.044). The executor kept driving the descent to its commanded pose, and the jam forced the seated parts and the fixture sideways, mostly in +y. This is part-on-part contact through the ACM-permitted channel, not an arm strike. The evidence does not settle which feature of inverted_u_yellow first contacted which seated part. The two unlisted objects (obs-001 cube at about (0.09, -0.37); obs-002 panel at about (0.23, -0.09), lying alongside base1's +y edge) are on record. The panel is close to where u_brown and base1 were pushed, but nothing I hold shows it caused the jam.

payload.explanation: Findings from fires still_u_orange_post2 (1793650246372029700), still_line_green_post (1793650246470944300) and still_u_brown_post3 (1793650246473964300), all within 0.1 s of each other during place_inverted_u_yellow. begin_step named u_orange, u_brown and line_green in object_ids as the seated mating parts the inverted U caps, so contact with them was permitted. Displacement beyond what seating requires was not. What I observed: all three had rested within 1-3 mm of their placement frames before the descent. At about 246.1 s, as inverted_u_yellow descended with its centre at z 0.083 (seat z 0.044), finger effort spiked from 63 to 115. u_orange was then thrown about 0.16-0.19 m to (0.346, -0.393, 0.015) and flipped over (orientation qx about 0.97, against a placement qx of -0.707). line_green was knocked 0.041 m and tilted about 16 deg. u_brown was pushed 0.035 m and now sits raised about 3 cm at z 0.075. Why it is a departure: none of this is something seating an inverted U requires. It destroyed three seats already established at their own milestones; each now fails its placement tolerance, measured after release against the frames, which moved with base1: u_brown 0.030 m vs 0.01 m, line_green about 0.036 m vs 0.015 m, u_orange about 0.19 m vs 0.02 m. What I believe happened: a collision. The carried inverted_u_yellow met the seated stack about 3.9 cm high and was driven through it under position control, ejecting u_orange off the -y side and shoving u_brown and line_green toward +y. The first contact point is not settled by the TF evidence. Frames are preserved under frames/u_orange_displaced_place_inverted_u_yellow_*.

payload.explanation: Finding from fire slip_inverted_u_yellow at trigger_wall_ns 1793650247426721300, during place_inverted_u_yellow, before release_skill started (1793650250636743200). What I observed: the tcp-frame offset of inverted_u_yellow had held at (-0.003, 0.000, 0.084) m from grasp confirmation through the pick, the transit and the place approach. At impact the part's world orientation swung from qx -0.706 to about -0.55, roughly 19 deg about x, and its centre stayed at z about 0.070 while the tcp kept descending from 0.163 to 0.128. Its tcp-frame position therefore moved 0.0209 m, over the 0.02 m slip tolerance. Finger effort spiked to 143 at about 247.93 s, while the finger position barely changed (0.4306 to 0.4295). Why it is a departure: the held part moved relative to the gripper before release. What I believe happened: this was not a weak grip slipping on its own. External contact with the seated stack blocked and rotated the part while the gripper continued its commanded descent, forcing it to rotate in the fingers. The part was then released tilted at z 0.068, 0.025 m from inverted_u_yellow_placement.

payload.explanation: End_step check at place_inverted_u_yellow, inverted_u_yellow's milestone. The executor claimed failure, and I agree. What I observed: after release, inverted_u_yellow is at (0.4053, -0.1768, 0.0675). Against the live inverted_u_yellow_placement frame (0.4087, -0.1686, 0.0444), the position error is 0.0248 m, beyond the 0.012 m position_m tolerance. The orientation is about 19 deg off about x (qx -0.582 vs -0.707), beyond the 10 deg orientation_deg tolerance. Note that the frame itself has moved about 0.031 m with base1; against its original pose the error is 0.033 m. The part is hung up about 2.3 cm high on the disturbed stack, not seated. The pick-side effects held: lift 0.30 m, effort plateau 77.6, the part tracked the tcp, and the width was consistent. Clamp effort peaked at about 143 during the collision, inside the 250 limit. Why it is a departure: the seat effect is the requirement due at this milestone, and it fails. What I believe happened: the same collision recorded in this step's three fire findings. The part met the seated stack about 3.9 cm above its seat during a position-controlled descent, was rotated in the fingers, and was released tilted on top of the displaced parts. Only the seat clauses here are new; the slip, displacement and base1 findings are already on the record and are not repeated.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict: non_conformant. All 12 steps were on the expected process. There were no unplanned and no reopened steps. The executor aborted after place_inverted_u_yellow, so no recovery was attempted.

Timeline: the first nine steps checked out clean on my own evidence.
- u_brown seated 0.0021 m from its frame (tolerance 0.01), u_orange 0.0024 m (tolerance 0.02) and line_green 0.0067 m (tolerance 0.015).
- Clamp efforts stayed far below each part's limit (60 of 100, 58 of 200, 16 of 170).
- No part slipped in hand.
- The only displacements were 1-3 mm nudges to base1 and to the named mating parts during seating, all far under the 0.02 m bound.
- pick_inverted_u_yellow and place_approach_inverted_u_yellow were also clean.

At place_inverted_u_yellow, the carried inverted_u_yellow met the seated stack about 3.9 cm above its seat height during a position-controlled descent, and was driven through it. That is part-on-part contact through the ACM-permitted channel. I recorded four findings under that step:
- base1 displaced (0.0207 m at the fire, 0.0315 m at run end).
- u_orange ejected about 0.19 m and flipped, and line_green and u_brown knocked 0.041 m and 0.035 m.
- inverted_u_yellow slipped 0.0209 m in the gripper as the contact rotated it about 19 deg.
- At end_step, inverted_u_yellow was not seated (0.0248 m, about 19 deg).
None of these was corrected.

End-state measured by me at run end, against the live placement frames (which moved about 0.031 m with base1):
- u_brown 0.0301 m (fails 0.01).
- u_orange 0.191 m, off the fixture and inverted (fails 0.02).
- line_green 0.0354 m, tilted about 16 deg (fails 0.015).
- inverted_u_yellow 0.0248 m (fails 0.012).
- base1 0.0315 m from its run-start pose (fails 0.02).
All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) are within 0.1 mm of their run-start poses, and their whole-run stationarity monitors never fired. Clamp effort never exceeded any limit; the peak was 143 of 250, during the collision.

The executor's own claim of failure and its abort agree with this. The verdict rests on my measurements, not on its status.

Workspace: two unlisted objects were recorded.
- obs-001: a ~5 cm orange-red cube that appeared at about (0.09, -0.37) during pick_u_orange and remained to run end without moving.
- obs-002: a ~0.44 x 0.09 m flat panel that appeared beside base1 during place_line_green and was gone by run end.
Neither is shown by my evidence to have caused a violation, and the panel's presence at the collision moment is not established.

Coverage and limitations:
- grasp_width_error_m relies on the executor-reported width, because no width calibration is readable. Finger positions corroborate contact in every grasp.
- object_tcp_offset_m was evaluated as the change in part-to-tcp offset after lift, because the tcp frame is not the grasp centre.
- base1's and base2's 0.02 m bound comes from the parts' raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m, since those fixtures have no contract of their own.
- I held the pick_u_orange 'grasped' phase gate about 45 s while investigating the cube, and the pick_inverted_u_yellow step gate about 35 s while characterising the panel. My first border-observation monitor was mis-armed (it fired on the arm's own link), so it was narrowed and re-armed; no verdict was recorded for that fire.
